newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Ortiz sees no sharp rate rise this year.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Ortiz sees no sharp rate rise this year.

text.p: Mexico's Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz on Thursday said that if Mexican interest rates rise he does not expect them to rise sharply.

"Most analysts expect that there will be perhaps some rebound toward mid-year, but not an excessive rise. To the extent that fundamental conditions of the international economy continue healthy, particularly in the United States, it is not expected that there is the risk of a very steep rise," Ortiz told reporters.
Mexican interest rates have fallen to to their lowest level since December 1994, when a peso devaluation plunged Mexico into economic crisis.
Bellwether 28-day Cetes rates this week fell for the 10th consecutive week to 18.59 percent.
Ortiz, speaking after a meeting to assess the progress of the government's anti-inflation pact with business and labor leaders, said he also did not expect a sharp rise in U.S. interest rates.
